title: Where to Buy Mobile Accessories Online in Pakistan
summary: Where to buy mobile accessories online in Pakistan: the five seller types compared, what to check on chargers and cables, and COD rules.
body_markdown:
Mobile accessories in Pakistan sell online through five kinds of seller: general marketplaces, official brand stores, Instagram and Facebook shops, reseller and wholesale platforms, and cross-border apps that ship from China. Each is priced differently and protects you differently. A marketplace is fastest for a case you need this week. A brand store is the safer route for a fast charger you plan to trust with an expensive phone. Social sellers are cheap and unpredictable. Wholesale platforms are built for people buying to resell. Cross-border apps carry the lowest stickers and the longest wait.


This guide sorts those channels by what you are actually buying, then covers the checks that matter for chargers, power banks, cables and earbuds — the categories where a bad online order costs you a phone rather than a few hundred rupees. If you are buying to resell instead of to use, the second half is written for you.


## The five places to buy mobile accessories online in Pakistan


Think of these as five different trades that happen to sell the same catalogue. Picking the wrong one is how people end up with a swollen power bank or a case that fits a different phone.


### 1. General marketplaces


Horizontal marketplaces carry the widest catalogue and the most sellers per product. That is both the strength and the trap. The same accessory shows up in ten listings at nine prices, and the listing photo is often the brand's press image rather than the item in that seller's box.


Buy here for low-risk items — cases, screen protectors, pop sockets, car mounts, ring holders — where a mismatch costs you a small amount and an argument. Read the **seller** rating, not just the product rating. On a shared product page the reviews can belong to a completely different seller's stock.


### 2. Official brand and authorised stores


Every serious accessory brand selling in Pakistan runs an official storefront or names its authorised dealers. This is the channel for anything that pushes current into your phone: fast chargers, wireless pads, car chargers, power banks, and the branded cables that go with them.


You pay more. What you get for the difference is a real warranty, a serial you can check, and a replacement path that does not depend on a WhatsApp number staying active. On a 25W charger for a phone that cost you six figures, that is a rational trade.


### 3. Instagram and Facebook sellers


Social selling is enormous in Pakistan and a lot of it is honest. It is also where the least accountable stock lives. There is no listing history, no dispute system, and no record of the transaction beyond a chat thread.


Rules that make this channel workable: insist on cash on delivery, ask for a video of the actual unit rather than a catalogue photo, and check whether the page has any comments left enabled. A page with comments disabled and only a highlights reel is telling you something.


### 4. Reseller and wholesale platforms


These exist for people buying stock rather than buying a phone case. Prices are reseller-tier instead of retail-tier, catalogues are organised by category rather than by brand, and the platform handles delivery and cash collection. Markaz sits here — you can browse the[Markaz product categories](https://www.markaz.app/shop/categories) to see how accessories are grouped and priced for resale.


The relevant point for an ordinary buyer: reseller platforms are usually where the accessory in a small local shop came from in the first place. Buying from one removes a markup layer, at the cost of a catalogue that is not built around consumer browsing.


### 5. Cross-border apps shipping from China


Cross-border apps show the lowest sticker prices you will see anywhere, because you are buying close to the factory tier with no importer in the middle. The trade-offs are consistent: you pay by card in a foreign currency, you wait through an international transit, customs can be billed on arrival, and returns are effectively theoretical. Our breakdown of[how cross-border shopping apps work in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/temu-in-pakistan-how-it-works-shipping-alternatives) walks the route leg by leg.


For a PKR 400 cable, the wait may be worth it. For a charger you need on Friday, it is not.


## What to check before you order


Mobile accessories are one of the few online categories where a bad purchase can damage something expensive. The checks differ by category.


### Chargers and adapters


Look for the actual output printed in the listing — wattage and the supported fast-charge standard — not the phrase "fast charger" on its own. A listing that will not state output is hiding a slow brick with a bright box. Check that the plug is a Pakistani-standard two-pin round or that an adapter is included, and that the body carries a brand name, a model number and safety marks.


### Power banks


Two numbers matter and both get exaggerated: capacity in mAh and output in watts. Weight is a useful sanity check — cells have mass, so a large-capacity pack that feels light is not what the label says. Buy this category from a brand store or an established seller. A failing power bank is a fire risk in a bag, not an inconvenience.


### Cables


Match the connector, the standard and the length before price. A USB-C cable that only carries the older charging standard will charge a modern phone slowly and never tell you why. Braided sleeves last longer than plain PVC in daily use. Cables are cheap enough that buying two from a known brand beats buying five unbranded ones.


### Earbuds and audio


Check the Bluetooth version, the claimed battery life per charge, and whether the case charges over USB-C. Ignore stated driver sizes; they are marketing. Read reviews that mention *call* quality specifically — cheap earbuds are usually acceptable for music and poor on the microphone, which is what most people actually use them for.


### Cases and screen protectors


The only real risk is fitment. Order by the exact model name and generation, not the family. Phone makers move camera modules between generations of the same line, and a case for last year's model will cover this year's lens. For tempered glass, check whether the listing includes an alignment frame — that one detail is the difference between a clean fit and a bubble along one edge.


## How to tell a real accessory from a rebadged one


Pakistan's accessory market carries three tiers that look identical in photos: branded stock, honest unbranded stock, and counterfeit stock pretending to be branded. The middle tier is fine and often good value. The third tier is the problem.


- **The price gap is the loudest signal.** A genuine branded charger sold far below what every authorised dealer charges is not a deal, it is a different product in a copied box.
- **Packaging print quality.** Counterfeit boxes get the artwork right and the small print wrong — misaligned text, missing model numbers, no safety marks.
- **Ask for the box photo before dispatch.** An honest seller sends it. This one request filters out a surprising share of bad orders.
- **Check the warranty claim against reality.** "One year warranty" from a seller with no shopfront and no service centre means the seller replaces it if they feel like it.
- **Unbranded is not fake.** A generic cable sold as a generic cable at a generic price is a legitimate purchase. The dishonesty is in the badge, not the absence of one.


## Cash on delivery, prepaid, and what each protects


Most accessory orders in Pakistan are cash on delivery, and that habit exists for a good reason: it moves the risk to the seller. You do not pay for a parcel that never arrives.


What COD does not do is let you inspect the item. Many couriers deliver on a pay-first basis, so you hand over cash and open the box afterwards. If open-parcel delivery matters to you, confirm it with the seller in writing before dispatch and keep the message.


Prepaid is worth it in exactly two cases: an official brand store where the transaction is recorded and warrantied, and a genuine discount large enough to price in the risk. On an unfamiliar social-media page, prepaying is simply donating.


## Buying mobile accessories to resell


Accessories are one of the most common entry categories for new sellers in Pakistan, and the reasons are structural. Unit prices are low, so the cost of a mistake is small. Every phone owner is a potential customer. Replacement cycles are short — cables fray, cases crack, earbuds get lost. And the category ships cheaply because almost nothing in it is heavy or fragile.


The pressure is on margin. Accessories are transparently priced, so buyers compare easily and the difference between profit and no profit is what you paid for the stock. Our guide to the[best gadgets and accessories to dropship in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-gadgets-accessories-to-dropship-in-pakistan) covers which sub-categories hold their margin.


### Where reseller pricing actually comes from


Retail prices for accessories in Pakistan carry several layers: importer, distributor, wholesaler, shop. A reseller buying at retail and selling at retail has nothing left. The job is to buy at a tier the end customer cannot access, which is what wholesale platforms and direct sourcing are for. We break the tiers down in[factory-price wholesale for Pakistani resellers](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/factory-price-wholesale-lowest-rates-for-pakistani-resellers) .

That inverts the usual problem for a new seller — you are not holding a carton of cases hoping the model stays current. Local orders deliver in 3–5 days and cash is collected on your behalf.

Most accessories sold in Pakistan originate in China regardless of which channel you buy through. Importing directly gets you the best unit price and hands you the parts nobody enjoys: minimum quantities, forwarders, customs paperwork and prepayment in a foreign currency.

## What to buy online and what to buy in person


Not everything belongs online. A rough split that holds up:


- **Buy online:** cases, screen protectors, cables, car mounts, stands, ring lights, smartwatch straps, replacement earbud tips, pop sockets. Low value, low risk, and the online catalogue is far deeper than any single shop.
- **Buy online from a brand store only:** fast chargers, wireless charging pads, power banks, branded earbuds. Warranty is the product here as much as the hardware.
- **Buy in person if you can:** anything that must fit a specific older or less common phone model, and anything you want to hear or hold first — over-ear headphones especially.


If you are shopping on price across categories rather than for one item,[cheapest online shopping in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/cheapest-online-shopping-in-pakistan) compares the channels on total landed cost rather than sticker price.


## A buying checklist


1. Name the exact phone model and generation before you search.
2. For anything electrical, find the stated output. No output stated, no order.
3. Compare the delivered total, including any delivery charge, not the listing price.
4. Check the seller's rating and history, not only the product's.
5. Default to cash on delivery unless the seller is an official store.
6. Ask for a photo of the actual unit and box before dispatch.
7. Screenshot the listing and the chat. It is the only warranty documentation you will have.
8. If you are buying to resell, price your margin off the tier you bought at — not off what the shop down the road charges.


## Frequently asked questions


### Where is the cheapest place to buy mobile accessories online in Pakistan?


On sticker price, cross-border apps shipping from China. On price you can actually use this week, wholesale and reseller platforms, because they cut out the retail markup while still delivering locally. General marketplaces sit between the two and vary seller by seller.


### Is it safe to buy a charger or power bank online?


Yes, from an official brand store or an established seller with a real returns process. Buying a no-name high-wattage charger from an anonymous page is the one purchase in this category genuinely worth avoiding — a bad charger can damage the phone it is plugged into.


### Can I get mobile accessories with cash on delivery?


Almost always. COD is the default for accessories across Pakistani marketplaces, social sellers and reseller platforms. Confirm before you order whether the courier allows you to open the parcel before paying, as that varies.


### How long does delivery usually take?


Stock already in Pakistan generally reaches you within a few days — on Markaz, 3–5 days for local orders. Anything shipping from China takes considerably longer; Markaz China orders arrive in about 10–17 days, and unmanaged cross-border parcels can take longer still.


### Are mobile accessories a good category to start reselling?


They are one of the better starting categories. Low unit cost, constant replacement demand, cheap to ship, and no size or colour matrix to manage the way clothing has. The catch is margin discipline: buy at a reseller tier or the numbers do not work.


### How do I know an accessory will fit my phone?


Match the full model name including the generation and any suffix, and read the compatibility line in the listing rather than assuming from the photo. For cases, the camera cutout is where mismatches show up first, since manufacturers move the module between generations of the same series.


### Do I need to buy in bulk to resell accessories?


Not on a no-minimum platform. Markaz has no minimum order quantity, so you can list products first and order a single unit once a customer buys — which is how most new resellers avoid putting money into stock that may not move.
